name: Recof Data - Recof M&A Database (レコフM&Aデータベース) / MARR Pro / MARR Online
data_types: Japan-related M&A deal records: deal announcements, acquirer/target/seller, deal form (acquisition, capital participation, share exchange, business transfer, split/carve-out, holding-company formation, going-private), deal values, TOB (tender offer) detail, fund/PE involvement, takeover defence measures, scheme-level detail, ADVISOR/agent information (option), treasury share buybacks, activist/carve-out flags, deal abstracts (案件抄録), plus M&A news and MARR magazine editorial/statistics. Business alliances are explicitly EXCLUDED from the deal universe. Attached EDINET disclosure documents downloadable as ZIP.
coverage_geo: Japan-centric: any deal involving a Japanese company (IN-IN, IN-OUT, OUT-IN) plus 'foreign-company-related transactions' as a standard category. Not a global M&A database. Publicly stated size: 'over 80,000 Japan-related M&A deals' (Recof press material, 2021). MARR Pro states '30 years' of data on its site.
history_depth: Recof M&A Database: 1985 onward (~40 years) - the canonical long-run Japanese M&A series. MARR Online paid membership gives reports built on data 'since 1985'. MARR Pro site says '30 years' and notes M&A速報 (news flash) browsable from 2017-09-01 onward. INFERRED: the deal table itself carries 1985+ history; the 2017 date applies only to the news-flash module.
api: No public REST API found. MARR Pro documents graph output as image or Excel, bulk Excel download for scheme-detail data, and ZIP download of disclosure documents. No API is mentioned on the MARR Pro or MARR Online pages. Docs URL: https://madb.recofdata.co.jp/help/index.html (legacy Recof DB help). CONFIRMED absence of published API docs; an OEM/data-feed arrangement may exist but is UNKNOWN.
bulk_delivery: Partial - Excel export and bulk Excel download of scheme-detail data inside MARR Pro; ZIP download of EDINET attachments. No SFTP/S3/Snowflake offering found. A raw bulk licence would have to be negotiated (UNKNOWN).
pricing: MARR Online (editorial + statistics portal, NOT the deal database): individual 1 user JPY 16,500/yr (~USD 110); corporate 5 users JPY 49,500/yr (~USD 330); 10 users JPY 82,500/yr (~USD 550); 11+ users JPY 41,250 per additional 5 users. Optional print MARR '統計とデータ編' JPY 33,000/yr, '記事編＋統計とデータ編' JPY 49,500/yr. Legacy pricing for pre-2025-05-31 contracts: 1 user JPY 16,500, 3 users JPY 33,000, 7 users JPY 66,000/yr. Source: https://www.marr.jp/memberPlan.html observed 2026-09. MARR Pro (the actual M&A database): QUOTE ONLY - annual contract, 1 licence = 5 named users, price varies by user count and optional modules (TOB detail, fund info, defence measures, scheme detail, treasury buybacks, advisor info). Source: https://www.marrpro.jp/ observed 2026-09. INFERENCE (not confirmed): a small-team MARR Pro licence is likely low-to-mid tier in JPY terms (historically Recof DB was quoted in the low millions of JPY per year), but no published figure exists - do not rely on this.
ml_training_license: Unknown. No public terms found addressing AI/ML training. Recof Data is a small Japanese publisher/data house; INFERRED HIGH RISK that a standard subscription forbids systematic extraction and model training, and that any ML use would need a bespoke data-licence negotiation. Must be confirmed directly with Recof Data.
language: Japanese only (interface and data). English-language page exists at https://www.marr.jp/english.html but the database itself is Japanese.
update_frequency: Every business day; new deals reflected 2 business days after public announcement (shortened from 3 business days in 2021).
fit_for_lead_prediction: The single best labelled outcome set for Japanese M&A - 1985+, 80k+ deals, consistent taxonomy, explicit acquirer/target identity - which is exactly what a target-prediction model needs as its positive labels. However there is no API and no bulk raw feed, so getting it into a training pipeline means negotiating a custom data licence rather than subscribing; and it carries no company-universe features (financials, ownership, president age), so it must be joined to TSR/TDB/gBizINFO data. Treat it as the label source, not the feature source.
budget_tier: unknown (MARR Online portal is low (<$10k/yr); MARR Pro database is quote-only, INFERRED low-to-mid for a small seat count)

name: SPEEDA (Uzabase) and SPEEDA RECOF
data_types: Company profiles and financials (listed and unlisted), industry/sector research reports, M&A transaction records, comparable-company and valuation data, news, executives, shareholder/ownership data, market data, Euromonitor market reports (bundled). SPEEDA RECOF adds the Recof Japanese M&A deal records surfaced on SPEEDA company/industry pages.
coverage_geo: Global. Vendor/third-party marketing states 200+ countries, 10 million+ companies and 1.8 million+ M&A transactions; another third-party summary cites 2.6 million+ M&A records worldwide. Domestic company-attribute dataset cited as ~1.5 million Japanese companies for sales use. NOTE: these counts come from third-party review sites and vendor LPs, not a machine-readable coverage document - treat as approximate.
history_depth: Not published. INFERRED: M&A records go back several decades via licensed third-party sources; SPEEDA RECOF inherits Recof's 1985+ Japanese history. Confirm with vendor.
api: Partial - yes, but as an integration/enrichment API, not a research-data API. Uzabase markets automatic API linkage to Salesforce, HubSpot, MA/SFA/CRM and ERP tools for real-time company-attribute enrichment and bulk back-population of historical data. No public developer documentation URL, no published rate limits, and no evidence the M&A deal table is exposed via API. Docs URL: not public.
bulk_delivery: Partial - Excel/CSV export from the UI is standard; a systematic bulk feed is not advertised. Format/scale of any bulk option is UNKNOWN.
pricing: Quote only - no public price list. Model is per-ID licence plus optional modules; cost varies with number of IDs, modules chosen, API/CRM integration option, and onboarding/training package. 7-day free trial then formal quote. SPEEDA RECOF is a SEPARATE paid add-on and requires BOTH a SPEEDA contract AND (formerly) a Recof M&A Database contract. Source: https://crexgroup.com/ja/data/column/data-ops/speeda-pricing-reviews-case-studies/ and https://www.itreview.jp/products/speeda/price (both THIRD-PARTY, observed 2026-09); https://www.marr.jp/speedarecof.html for the add-on structure. Third-party reviews commonly place SPEEDA in the JPY low-millions/yr for a small team, but NO figure is confirmed - do not quote a number.
ml_training_license: Unknown, and INFERRED restrictive. Much of SPEEDA's content is licensed in from third parties (Euromonitor, Recof, financial data vendors), which normally blocks sub-licensing for model training. Any AI/ML training use requires an explicit written carve-out. Note Uzabase now sells its own 'Speeda AI Agent', which suggests they intend to monetise AI use themselves rather than license training rights.
language: Japanese and English (SPEEDA has an English interface and English company/industry content); SPEEDA RECOF content is Japanese.
update_frequency: Continuous / daily for news and company data; not formally published per dataset.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Attractive because it is the one Asian platform that couples a large M&A transaction table with a broad company universe and financials in one contract, and it already ships a CRM-enrichment API - so it could feed a Salesforce-based lead-scoring workflow. The blockers are that the API is built for record-by-record enrichment rather than bulk historical extraction, and the heavy reliance on in-licensed third-party content makes an ML-training right unlikely without a bespoke deal. Best used as a feature-enrichment service for scored accounts, not as the training corpus.
budget_tier: unknown (INFERRED mid to enterprise once M&A module + API integration + SPEEDA RECOF are added)

name: Nikkei Value Search (日経バリューサーチ) / Nikkei Media Marketing
data_types: Company and industry analysis: company profiles, financials, business segments, industry reports and market maps, news (Nikkei Telecom article archive), competitor/peer comparison, catchment/market analysis, and supply-chain/relationship views. M&A deal data: NOT confirmed as a distinct product module. NOTE: Nikkei separately distributes 'Recof M&A information' (マールＭ＆Ａ情報) as a licensed database inside Nikkei Telecom (nikkei.com T21), and Nikkei Media Marketing separately resells Tokyo Shoko Research company data - so M&A deal records reach the Nikkei ecosystem via licensing rather than as native NVS content.
coverage_geo: Japan-centric with some overseas company coverage. Company counts not published on the pricing pages.
history_depth: Not published. Nikkei Telecom's article and Recof M&A modules carry long back-files (Recof module = 1985+ by inheritance). NVS depth UNKNOWN.
api: Partial/yes but undocumented publicly. The official NVS site states an API is provided and that integration with SFA/CRM/sales-support systems is possible, with details on inquiry. No public developer docs, no endpoint list, no rate limits published. Docs URL: not public (see https://nvs.nikkei.co.jp/sfa/faq/).
bulk_delivery: Unknown for NVS. Nikkei Media Marketing does broker bulk company-data deliveries (e.g. TSR data 'tailored to your needs'), so a file-based arrangement is plausible but unconfirmed.
pricing: Quote only. Official pages state: annual contract (no spot contracts), an initial/setup fee plus a monthly base fee, 'flat-fee unlimited use' with some metered or optional content, fully-fixed-fee packages available, concurrent-connection based licensing, 14-day free trial, same-day start possible. NO JPY figures are published on either the nvs.nikkei.co.jp/price/ or nikkeimm.co.jp/valuesearch/price/ pages (both checked 2026-09).
ml_training_license: Unknown, and INFERRED restrictive. NVS bundles Nikkei newspaper article content and licensed third-party company data; Nikkei's article licensing is historically strict and text/data-mining rights are normally excluded. Assume no ML training right without a separate written licence.
language: Japanese (primary). Some English company data; interface is Japanese.
update_frequency: Daily for news; company/financial data updated on filing cycles. Not formally published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Weak as a training corpus and moderate as a feature source. It is a research/analysis workbench rather than a structured deal database, M&A transactions are not a confirmed native module, and everything is quote-only with an undocumented API. Its real value to a Japanese advisory firm is the CRM-integration API for enriching an existing account list, plus the fact that Nikkei can bundle Recof M&A information and TSR company data under one commercial relationship - which may be worth a single conversation covering all three.
budget_tier: unknown (INFERRED mid; Nikkei enterprise information products typically land in the JPY low-millions/yr for a team, unconfirmed)

name: Tokyo Shoko Research (TSR / 東京商工リサーチ)
data_types: Private-company master data: trade name, corporate number, address, phone, TSR credit score (評点), listing status, incorporation date, capital, employees, 3 years of revenue and profit, industry codes, representative/president details (name, age, background), officers, shareholders, bank relationships, business description, full financial statements (BS/PL), TSR credit investigation reports, bankruptcy-risk score (1-100), and establishment/office-level data. Also runs an 'online matching' function inside the API service. NOT an M&A deal database - this is the company-universe/feature side.
coverage_geo: Japan: 'over 10 million' company records (largest domestic scale per vendor); 'over 7 million' Japanese companies plus 'over 600 million' worldwide entities accessible via the tsr-van2 web service (the global part is via partner/D&B-style networks). Establishment-level file (事業所情報ファイル) available separately.
history_depth: Standard delivery carries 3 fiscal years of revenue/profit per company. Longer time series and point-in-time snapshots are not advertised - INFERRED that historical panel data would need a custom arrangement. This matters: without point-in-time snapshots you cannot cleanly build features 'as of' a past deal date.
api: Yes - 'TSR API連携サービス' (launched 2016-11-01). TSR supplies a specification document and credentials and the customer builds against it; test environment allows XML and PDF retrieval free of charge. Response formats include XML and PDF. Protocol not explicitly labelled REST on the page. Docs URL: https://www.tsr-net.co.jp/service/detail/api.html (spec issued under contract, not public).
bulk_delivery: Yes - this is TSR's strength. 'TSR企業情報ファイル' / 'TSR営業支援ファイル' deliver flat database files in fixed-width layouts (3300, 1900, 1046, 540, 283, 211 bytes per record) for a chosen company list or filter.
pricing: PUBLISHED and unusually transparent for bulk. Extraction/matching base fee per delivery: 1-2,500 companies JPY 50,000; 2,501-5,000 JPY 100,000; 5,001+ JPY 300,000. Per-company information fee by layout and volume, e.g. 3300-byte layout: 500 companies (flat) JPY 250/company, 501-1,000 JPY 250, 1,001-3,000 JPY 230, declining with volume, 100,001+ by negotiation. Cheapest tier observed: 211-byte layout at 100,001+ companies = JPY 15/company. Worked example on TSR's own page: 211-byte x 1,000 companies = JPY 110,000 total (JPY 50,000 base + JPY 60,000 data). tsr-van2 ad-hoc web lookups: JPY 1,200 per record. TSR API service: quote only ('price varies by development content and usage form'). Sources: https://www.tsr-net.co.jp/service/detail/data-package.html and https://www.tsr-net.co.jp/service/detail/tsr-van2.html, observed 2026-09. IMPLIED BUDGET MATH (my calculation, not a quote): 100,000 companies at the 211-byte JPY 15 rate + JPY 300,000 base = approx JPY 1.8M (~USD 12,000) one-off; 100,000 companies at a JPY 150-230 richer layout would be JPY 15M-23M (~USD 100k-155k) and blows the budget. So richness-vs-volume is the key negotiating axis.
ml_training_license: Unknown. Not addressed on public pages. TSR files are normally licensed for a stated internal purpose with per-delivery pricing, which INFERS that model training would be treated as a new use case requiring explicit permission. Because TSR prices per record and per delivery, a training-corpus licence is a realistic thing to ask for and to price - worth a direct request.
language: Japanese.
update_frequency: Rolling - TSR continuously re-surveys companies; file deliveries are point-in-time per order, with periodic refresh deliveries possible. Exact cadence per field not published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: This is the strongest realistic FEATURE source in Japan for the specific signals the firm cares about - president age, successor absence proxies, employee/revenue trajectory, credit score deterioration, capital and shareholder structure - across the private-company universe where Japanese mid-market M&A actually happens. The published per-record pricing makes a budget-bounded bulk purchase genuinely possible (unlike TDB), and the byte-layout tiers let you trade field richness against volume. Main gaps: only 3 years of financials as standard and no advertised point-in-time history, so ask specifically for historical snapshots or you cannot build leak-free training features.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) to mid ($10k-50k/yr) depending on volume and layout richness; enterprise if you want rich layouts at 100k+ companies

name: Teikoku Databank (TDB / 帝国データバンク) - COSMOS2 / COSMOSNET API
data_types: COSMOS2 is TDB's company-profile database: approximately 40 fields covering all industries - trade name, address, corporate number, industry, incorporation, capital, employees, revenue and profit, representative (name, DOB/age, background), officers, shareholders, banks, main customers/suppliers, TDB credit score (評点). COSMOS2 Full (フル) adds further detail. Separate products: TDB credit investigation reports (信用調査), financial databases (COSMOS1), and an English-language 英文COSMOS2. NOT an M&A deal database.
coverage_geo: Japan - marketed as 'Japan's largest-class company profile database'. Vendor cites all industries nationwide. Exact record count not captured on the pages checked (commonly stated as ~1.4-1.6 million profiled companies; NOT CONFIRMED here).
history_depth: Point-in-time profiles with a small number of fiscal years of results; TDB holds long internal survey history but historical panel delivery is not a published product. UNKNOWN.
api: Yes - 'COSMOSNET API サービス' lets a customer's system query TDB's database directly and retrieve company information in real time. Pre-built connectors exist for kintone (free plugin, requires a separate COSMOS2 data contract) and UiPath. Docs URL: https://www.tdb.co.jp/services/lineup/api/ (spec under contract, not public).
bulk_delivery: Yes - disk/file delivery of COSMOS2 data is a priced option (see pricing), alongside paper report delivery. Formats not specified publicly.
pricing: PUBLISHED per-record. COSMOS2 基本 (basic): JPY 1,200 per company (excl. tax). COSMOS2 フル (full): JPY 1,600 per company. Plus a base fee: JPY 10,000 for paper products, JPY 50,000 for disk/file products, in each case on top of the per-record data fee. Source: https://www.tdb.co.jp/lineup/cnet/cnetdemo/HTML/TA412F01.html and https://www.tdb.co.jp/lineup/cnet/cnetdemo/HTML/TA231F01_N.html, observed 2026-09. CRITICAL BUDGET NOTE: at JPY 1,200/company with no visible volume discount, 10,000 companies = JPY 12M (~USD 80,000) and 100,000 companies = JPY 120M (~USD 800,000). This pricing is structurally incompatible with a sub-USD-50k bulk training-set purchase. Volume discounts almost certainly exist under negotiation but are NOT published - do not assume them.
ml_training_license: Unknown. Not addressed publicly. INFERRED very restrictive: TDB's per-record, per-purpose commercial model and its credit-reporting regulatory posture make blanket ML-training rights unlikely without a bespoke and expensive licence.
language: Japanese; an English-language product (英文COSMOS2) exists.
update_frequency: Continuous re-survey; API returns real-time current records. Cadence per field not published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Field-for-field TDB is arguably the highest-quality Japanese private-company dataset and includes the president-age and successor signals that drive Japanese succession-driven M&A. But the published per-record price of JPY 1,200-1,600 makes bulk acquisition for model training economically impossible at this budget - it is priced for one-at-a-time credit checking, not for corpus building. Realistic use is a real-time API lookup on already-shortlisted targets, with TSR or gBizINFO carrying the bulk universe. Compare directly against TSR, which publishes volume tiers down to JPY 15/record.
budget_tier: enterprise (>$50k/yr) for any training-scale volume; low for occasional single-record API lookups

name: J-Quants API (JPX Market Innovation & Research / JPX総研) - retail tier
data_types: Japanese listed-market data via API: listed issue master, daily OHLCV, financial statements, dividends, investor-category trading flows, index data, morning/afternoon session quotes (premium), margin/short data, and - per a 2026-05-18 JPX release headline - timely-disclosure (適時開示) data was added to J-Quants API. A 2026-01-19 release headline indicates CSV-format provision was added. NOTE: the two 2026 additions are read from JPX release TITLES only (the release pages returned HTTP 403); content unverified.
coverage_geo: Japan listed equities only (TSE/JPX). ~4,000 listed companies. No private-company and no deal-level M&A data.
history_depth: By plan: Free = 2 years (delivered with a 12-week lag); Light = 5 years; Standard = 10 years; Premium = full available history.
api: Yes - REST/JSON with token auth. Rate limits by plan: Free 5 requests/min, Light 60/min, Standard 120/min, Premium 500/min. Docs URL: https://jpx-jquants.com/ja/spec and https://jpx-jquants.com/ja/spec/data-spec.
bulk_delivery: Partial - CSV-format provision was announced (2026-01-19 release title). Primary access is API. No SFTP/S3/Snowflake.
pricing: PUBLISHED (tax incl.): Free JPY 0; Light JPY 1,650/month (~USD 11); Standard JPY 3,300/month (~USD 22); Premium JPY 16,500/month (~USD 110, approx USD 1,300/yr). Minute/tick data add-on JPY 5,500/month, available to Light and above. Source: https://jpx-jquants.com/ja/help/plan and the plan table at https://jpx-jquants.com/ja/#pricing, observed 2026-09.
ml_training_license: EXPLICITLY DISALLOWED for this firm's use case. Official terms state the service is limited to private use by INDIVIDUALS; use by corporations is prohibited, as is third-party redistribution of the data or provision of apps built on it, whether for profit or not. 'Private use' is defined as one's own investment analysis and portfolio management, and repeatedly providing analysis results to third parties does not qualify. JPX explicitly directs corporate and academic-research users to J-Quants Pro. Source: https://jpx-jquants.com/ja/help/usage. CONCLUSION: JCAI cannot lawfully use the retail J-Quants API - go to J-Quants Pro.
language: Japanese and English (docs available in both).
update_frequency: Daily (Free tier is delayed 12 weeks).
fit_for_lead_prediction: Cheap and technically clean, and the newly added timely-disclosure feed would be a useful real-time trigger source for listed-company M&A events. But it is legally unusable here: the terms bar corporate use outright, so evaluating it for a firm pipeline is a dead end. Its only legitimate role is as a personal prototyping sandbox for an individual engineer, and even the resulting model could not be deployed commercially. Route the requirement to J-Quants Pro.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) but LICENCE-INELIGIBLE for corporate use

Internal use, single legal entity (単一法人利用): listed issue master JPY 50,000/month (~USD 330); investor-category trading information JPY 20,000/month (~USD 130). Internal use, group companies (系列法人利用): listed issue master JPY 130,000/month (~USD 870); investor-category trading information JPY 40,000/month (~USD 270). Source: JPX press releases at https://www.jpx.co.jp/corporate/news/news-releases/6020/20240215-01.html and the J-Quants Pro site, observed 2026-09 (note: the JPX release HTML returned 403 to direct fetch; figures come from the indexed release content and the accompanying PDF at .../skc8fn0000001mzk-att/press_release.pdf).

JPX explicitly names corporate use AND academic research as the intended J-Quants Pro use cases, and prices an explicit 'internal use' licence scope - which is the right shape for internal model training. Redistribution/external distribution is a separate, more expensive licence class. Whether 'internal use' extends to training a model whose OUTPUT is used commercially is NOT stated - get this in writing.
language: Japanese and English.
update_frequency: Daily / per dataset publication cycle.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The right legal channel for JPX listed-market data, with genuinely cheap per-dataset pricing and an explicit internal-use licence - a few datasets for a single entity would run roughly USD 5k-15k/yr. Its limitation is scope: listed companies only, no deal records, so it contributes acquirer-side features (who has balance-sheet capacity, shareholding structure, disclosure behaviour) rather than target labels. Pair with TDnet or EDINET for the M&A event stream and with TSR for the private-company universe.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for one or two datasets, single-entity internal use; mid if several datasets or group-wide licence

name: TDnet timely disclosure (JPX / JPX総研 paid data services)
data_types: Full timely-disclosure filings from all Japanese listed companies - the primary real-time source for announced M&A by listed issuers (share acquisitions, tender offers, business transfers, capital and business alliances, subsidiary transfers, share exchanges/transfers, MBO/going-private announcements), plus earnings, forecast revisions, dividends, governance and other disclosures. Delivered as disclosure documents plus metadata (company code, disclosure time, title, category).
coverage_geo: Japan - all TSE/JPX listed companies (~4,000 issuers). Regional exchanges mirror the viewing service.
history_depth: JPX's free public website retains only 31 days of disclosures. The paid TDnet Database Service (TDnetDBS) is the historical archive product; exact back-file start not captured - REQUEST from JPX. TDnet has operated since the early 2000s, so INFERRED ~20+ years of archive.
api: Yes - 'TDnet API サービス'. Also available as a server-type push feed, a database service (TDnetDBS), and 'TDnet on Snowflake'. Docs URL: https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/paid-info-listing/tdnet/02.html ; service guide PDF https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/paid-info-listing/tdnet/co3pgt0000005o97-att/TDnetAPI_ServiceGuide.pdf ; terms PDF https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/paid-info-listing/tdnet/co3pgt0000005o97-att/TermsTDAPIJ.pdf
bulk_delivery: Yes - TDnet Database Service, server-type feed, and notably TDnet on Snowflake (a genuine warehouse-native delivery, which is unusual and valuable for ML work).
pricing: PUBLISHED (all excl. tax unless noted). TDnet API: base JPY 70,000/month (~USD 470) PLUS a tiered API information fee based on documents retrieved that month - up to 300 docs: JPY 0; 301-2,000: JPY 50,000; 2,001-15,000: JPY 170,000; 15,001+: JPY 170,000 plus JPY 100,000 for each additional 15,000 docs. TDnet Database Service: JPY 36,740/month per ID (tax included). TDnet server-type: JPY 200,000 initial per line + JPY 230,000/month information fee + JPY 10,000/month line maintenance. TDnet on Snowflake: from JPY 100,000/month (~USD 670). Free: 31 days of disclosures on the JPX website. Sources: https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/paid-info-listing/tdnet/02.html , /01.html , and the index page, observed 2026-09. BUDGET MATH (my calculation): Japanese listed companies produce well over 15,000 disclosures/month in aggregate, so a full-firehose API subscription would run roughly JPX 70,000 + 170,000+ per month = JPY 240,000+/month (~USD 19,000+/yr) and rise steeply; a filtered subscription retrieving only M&A-category documents could sit in the JPY 70,000-120,000/month band (~USD 5,600-9,600/yr). Verify the fee is on documents RETRIEVED, not documents published.
ml_training_license: Unknown - a formal terms document exists (TDnet API サービス利用約款, PDF linked above) and should be read directly. INFERRED: JPX distinguishes internal use from redistribution (as it does for J-Quants Pro), so internal analytics/model training is plausibly permissible while redistributing derived disclosure content is not. Confirm in the 約款.
language: Japanese (disclosure documents; a subset of issuers file English versions).
update_frequency: Real time - disclosures are available at the moment of publication.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Excellent as the EVENT/LABEL stream for listed-company M&A in Japan: it is the authoritative, timestamped, real-time source, and the Snowflake delivery option from JPY 100,000/month is a rare warehouse-native feed at a plausible price. Two caveats: it covers only listed issuers, so it misses the unlisted-target side of most Japanese mid-market deals, and the documents are unstructured Japanese PDFs/XBRL requiring NLP extraction to become structured deal records. Cheapest sane design is Snowflake or a category-filtered API pull, with Recof/MARR used to validate extraction accuracy.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for Snowflake entry tier or a tightly filtered API pull; mid ($10k-50k/yr) for a full API firehose or server-type feed

name: EDINET API (Financial Services Agency, Japan)
data_types: Statutory disclosure filings for Japanese issuers: annual securities reports (有価証券報告書), quarterly/semi-annual reports, extraordinary reports (臨時報告書 - which is where material acquisitions/disposals of subsidiaries are reported), tender offer notifications (公開買付届出書) and tender offer reports, large shareholding reports (大量保有報告書 - the 5%+ rule, a direct pre-M&A stake-building signal), share exchange/transfer and merger registration statements, and prospectuses. Filings are available as XBRL, plus PDF and attachment ZIPs. Structured financial data comes via XBRL taxonomy.
coverage_geo: Japan - all EDINET filers: listed companies plus unlisted issuers with disclosure obligations, funds, and foreign issuers filing in Japan.
history_depth:
CORRECTION (2026-09-03, verified against FIEA Art. 25 via e-Gov and EDINET API spec v2.9): extraordinary reports are viewable 5 YEARS (not 1 year; 1 year applies to the treasury-stock repurchase report). Annual / semi-annual / quarterly reports 10 years; tender-offer filings 5 years from end of offer period; 5% reports 5 years; list API accepts dates back 10 years. Original researcher text follows.

EDINET holds filings from roughly 2008 onward for the current system, with earlier material in the legacy archive. The API's document-list endpoint is documented for retrieval by date. Exact API-accessible window: verify in the spec (Version 2, June 2026 edition).
api: Yes - EDINET API Version 2, requiring an API key. Documented endpoints: document list API (書類一覧API) and document acquisition API (書類取得API). Specification PDF: https://disclosure2dl.edinet-fsa.go.jp/guide/static/disclosure/download/ESE140206.pdf (Version 2, 2026-06, FSA).
bulk_delivery: Partial - no SFTP/S3, but the document-list API by date plus the document-acquisition API allows systematic date-range harvesting into your own store, which is functionally bulk. XBRL and ZIP downloads supported.
pricing: FREE - no fee for the API or an API key. No published price because there is none. Source: FSA EDINET API specification and the EDINET site, observed 2026-09. (One third-party commentary page, https://gxceed.com/edinet-api , discusses fees/'料金' and XBRL parsing caveats; the API itself is free.)
ml_training_license: Favourable but with operational limits. The EDINET terms of use permit API access but PROHIBIT scraping and excessive/mass access, and reserve the right to suspend the API. The filings themselves are statutory public disclosures, which INFERS wide latitude for internal analytical and model-training use; there is no known clause forbidding ML training. Practical constraint is throughput, not licence. Confirm against the current 利用規約.
language: Japanese (a subset of filings have English versions; XBRL element labels available in English).
update_frequency: Real time as filings are submitted; business-day cycle.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The best free structured source in Japan and a genuine budget anchor. Two filing types are directly predictive rather than merely descriptive: 大量保有報告書 (5%+ shareholding reports) reveal stake-building BEFORE a bid, and 臨時報告書 record subsidiary acquisitions and disposals - both are strong leading indicators, and XBRL gives you clean multi-year financials for free. Costs are engineering (XBRL parsing, Japanese NLP, rate-limit-respectful harvesting) rather than licence fees. Build this first before paying anyone, because it also gives you a free baseline to measure whether Recof or TDnet actually add lift.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) - zero licence cost, engineering effort only

name: gBizINFO (Gビズインフォ, METI - Japan Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry)
data_types: Government-held corporate data keyed on the Japanese corporate number (法人番号): corporate basic information (name, address, corporate number, industry, capital, employees, establishment date), subsidy/grant awards (補助金情報), filings and certifications (届出・認定情報), commendations (表彰情報), procurement/contract awards (調達情報), patent information (特許情報), financial information (財務情報), workplace information (職場情報 - hiring, turnover, childcare-leave and training data), and survey information.
coverage_geo: Japan - 'over 5 million' corporate entities (all registered Japanese corporations with a corporate number), per third-party summary. This is the widest Japanese company universe available and includes the long tail of small companies that commercial databases skip.
history_depth: Varies by dataset. Subsidy, procurement and certification records accumulate over multiple years (roughly 2010s onward for the digitised series); corporate basic info is current-state. Not uniformly documented - INFERRED.
api: Yes - free REST API returning JSON, token-authenticated. Endpoints support search by criteria and retrieval by corporate number, across the datasets listed above. Docs URL: https://info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/APIManual ; Swagger UI: https://api.info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/swagger-ui/index.html ; also catalogued at https://api-catalog.e-gov.go.jp/info/ja/apicatalog/view/65
bulk_delivery: Yes - a bulk download section exists at https://info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/DownloadTop (CSV-style downloads). Exact file inventory and terms not verified in this pass.
pricing: FREE - all functions are free of charge. API token is obtained by application (individuals need only an email address and a stated purpose; token typically arrives same-day to within a few hours). Sources: https://info.gbiz.go.jp/hojin/APIManual (official) and https://salesnow.jp/media/176/ plus https://salesnow.jp/media/34/ (THIRD-PARTY summaries, observed 2026-09).
ml_training_license: Likely permissive but VERIFY. A third-party guide states commercial use is permitted subject to API token application. The official site references an 'API・データダウンロード利用規約' whose specific licence (e.g. whether it follows the Japanese Government Standard Terms of Use / CC-BY compatibility) was NOT confirmed in this pass. Japanese government open data is normally CC-BY-compatible, which would allow ML training with attribution - but read the 利用規約 before relying on it. INFERRED favourable.
language: Japanese (some English metadata).
update_frequency: Varies by dataset; corporate basic information syncs with the National Tax Agency corporate-number registry, subsidy and procurement data update on award cycles. Not uniformly published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The best free way to build the Japanese company UNIVERSE and the negative/unlabelled class for a target-prediction model - 5 million+ entities with corporate numbers, which also gives you the join key to link TSR, TDB, EDINET and your own CRM. Some fields are unexpectedly predictive: subsidy and procurement history proxy for growth and government dependence, and workplace/turnover data proxies for organisational stress. It lacks president age, succession status and credit scores, so it cannot replace TSR - use gBizINFO as the free spine and buy paid enrichment only for the shortlist the model surfaces.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) - free

name: Baseconnect - Musubu (ムスブ) and PARTNERSHIP API
data_types: Japanese company master data aimed at B2B sales: company name, corporate number, HQ and branch/office addresses, phone, industry, capital, employees, revenue band, establishment year, business description, website, listing status, and contact-form URLs. Includes email/outreach features. NO M&A deal data, NO credit scores, NO president-age or succession fields, NO detailed financial statements.
coverage_geo: Japan - 'over 1.4 million' Japanese company records covering HQ and establishments (vendor claim, PR release states 'over 1 million' at launch). Used by 76,000+ companies per vendor.
history_depth: Current-state only. No historical panel. Not suitable as a time-series feature source.
api: Yes - Baseconnect operates 'PARTNERSHIP API', a data-provider service supplying company information via API integration to partners. Musubu itself also integrates with CRM/SFA tools. Docs URL: not public; PARTNERSHIP API is a B2B partnership offering requiring direct contact.
bulk_delivery: Partial - Musubu exports company lists (CSV) subject to a monthly record-unlock quota; the PARTNERSHIP API is the route to larger volumes. No SFTP/S3/Snowflake advertised.
pricing: Musubu SaaS plans (THIRD-PARTY SOURCED, figures vary between review sites - treat as indicative, observed 2026-09): Free plan JPY 0 with 30 company records downloadable; 3-month start plan approx JPY 55,000/month; 6-month plan approx JPY 45,000-50,000/month with ~6,000 records and 18,000 emails over the term; 12-month plan from approx JPY 45,000/month; single-month plan approx JPY 60,000/month with 1,000 records and 2,000 emails; one source cites 'from JPY 25,000/month'. Initial fee JPY 0. Record top-up options: 100 records JPY 6,000; 500 records JPY 20,000; 1,000 records JPY 30,000 (i.e. JPY 30-60 per company, ~USD 0.20-0.40). Sources: https://saas.imitsu.jp/cate-company-database/service/3466/price , https://it-trend.jp/sfa/11910/price , https://www.itreview.jp/products/musubu/price , https://digi-mado.jp/products/45380/ - ALL THIRD-PARTY. Baseconnect has published a price-revision notice (https://company.baseconnect.in/news/63), so third-party figures may be stale. PARTNERSHIP API: quote only. A 12-month Musubu subscription is roughly JPY 540,000/yr (~USD 3,600).
ml_training_license: Unknown, and INFERRED restrictive for the SaaS product - Musubu is sold with an explicit monthly record-unlock quota, which is a licensing mechanism designed to prevent bulk extraction, so training on the full 1.4M universe via the SaaS tier would breach the commercial intent. The PARTNERSHIP API is the correct channel to ask about a bulk/derivative-use licence. Must confirm.
language: Japanese.
update_frequency: Continuous/rolling updates to the company database; cadence not published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Cheap and easy but thin for this purpose. The per-record top-up price of JPY 30-60 is roughly 20-40x cheaper than TDB, but the fields are sales-contact oriented and lack precisely the succession, credit and financial-trajectory variables that drive Japanese mid-market M&A - and there is no historical panel at all. Reasonable as a low-cost universe/contactability layer or as an outreach tool once the model has ranked targets; not a training corpus. Compare its PARTNERSHIP API against TSR's bulk file before choosing.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for the SaaS tiers; PARTNERSHIP API unknown

name: Wind Information (万得资讯 / Wind资讯)
data_types: Comprehensive Chinese financial data terminal (WFT): equities, bonds, futures, FX, funds, indices, macroeconomic and industry data, listed-company financials and ownership, corporate actions, M&A and equity-transfer transactions, IPO and issuance data, PMS portfolio management, research reports, and the iWind conference platform. M&A/corporate-transaction coverage is a module within a much larger terminal rather than a standalone deal database.
coverage_geo: China A-shares, HK, and global markets with China depth. Also covers Chinese unlisted equity transfers and state-asset transactions. Exact deal counts not published publicly.
history_depth: Long back-files for Chinese listed markets (INFERRED 1990s onward, matching the A-share market's history). Not publicly documented per dataset.
api: Yes - Wind Client API (WindPy for Python, plus Excel, MATLAB, R and C++ interfaces) for programmatic data extraction, available to terminal subscribers. Docs URL: https://www.wind.com.cn/portal/en/ClientApi/ and https://www.wind.com.cn/mobile/ClientApi/en.html . API access is generally bundled with or added to a terminal licence rather than sold as a standalone REST service.
bulk_delivery: Partial - Wind sells enterprise data feeds and database products (Wind Financial Database, WDS) to institutions, but these are negotiated enterprise arrangements. The Client API is rate-limited and intended for interactive/quant extraction, not full-corpus dumping.
pricing: Quote only - no public price list. THIRD-PARTY/INDIRECT data point: institutional users have been reported at an average annual billing of approximately CNY 87,000 (8.7万元, ~USD 12,000) per institutional customer; individual/small licences are described as ranging from tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of CNY per year. These figures come from a search-result summary of Chinese-language commentary (likely derived from Wind's IPO-related disclosures) and are NOT confirmed against a primary Wind document - treat as low confidence and do not quote to a client. Contact: 400-820-9463 / Service@wind.com.cn. Academic access is commonly provided via university library subscriptions (e.g. Sun Yat-sen, Xiamen, XJTLU).
ml_training_license: Unknown, and INFERRED restrictive. Chinese financial data terminals typically license per named seat with explicit prohibitions on systematic extraction, storage and derivative redistribution; Wind is known in the market for aggressive enforcement against bulk scraping. Additionally, Chinese data-export rules (PIPL, Data Security Law, cross-border data transfer measures) may constrain moving China-sourced datasets to a Japanese training environment - this is a legal question for qualified counsel, not an assumption.
language: Chinese (primary); English interface available.
update_frequency: Real time / 7x24x365 service.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The deepest China dataset by far and the only realistic single source for Chinese M&A plus company fundamentals, and a single institutional seat may sit near the middle of the stated budget. But it is architecturally wrong for this task: seat-licensed terminal access with a rate-limited API, no bulk export right, and an INFERRED prohibition on the systematic extraction that model training requires - plus a genuine cross-border data-transfer question for a Japanese firm. Treat as a China research tool for advisers, not as a training-data supplier, unless Wind will quote an explicit data-licence.
budget_tier: mid ($10k-50k/yr) for terminal seats based on the unconfirmed CNY 87,000 average; enterprise (>$50k/yr) for any bulk data-feed licence (INFERRED)

Worth one direct enquiry to test whether they will quote a data licence rather than seats, but do not plan around the CNY 58,000 figure.

name: ITjuzi (IT桔子)
data_types: China new-economy/TMT primary-market database: investment and financing events, M&A events, IPO events, startup and notable-company profiles, investment institutions (VC/PE/CVC), key people/founders, industry research reports, and investment news. Explicitly includes daily risk-investment, M&A and IPO information as one of its four data pillars.
coverage_geo: China, TMT and new-economy focused (not all-industry). Vendor/third-party counts vary by source and vintage: '500,000+ companies, financing events, institutions and people' in one place; '160,000+ company records, 80,000+ investment/financing events, 8,000+ institutions, 60,000+ research reports' in another. Treat as order-of-magnitude. Customer list includes Tencent, Alibaba, Baidu and ByteDance as data buyers, which is a meaningful credibility signal for its enterprise data business.
history_depth: Launched 2013-05-21 and describes itself as the earliest Chinese commercial data company focused on primary-market venture data - so INFERRED ~2013 onward for natively collected data, with some backfill. Not published.
api: Yes - ITjuzi explicitly offers API access as part of its enterprise data service, noting it requires technical engineering resources on the customer side, alongside monthly Excel summaries and custom delivery. Docs URL: not public; contact hello@itjuzi.com . User documentation (product usage, not API): https://static.itjuzi.com/itjuzi-user-document-2.2.pdf
bulk_delivery: YES - and this is the notable finding. ITjuzi's enterprise service explicitly supports on-demand cleaning and field filtering with delivery in Excel, CSV, MySQL and JSON formats, plus incremental database updates on daily, weekly, monthly or quarterly cycles. That is an unusually ML-friendly delivery menu for an Asian deal database - a MySQL dump with incremental refresh is close to ideal for a training pipeline.
pricing: PUBLISHED for individual membership: monthly CNY 108 (~USD 15); quarterly CNY 298 (~USD 41); annual CNY 798 (~USD 110). Source: ITjuzi site/app store listings, observed 2026-09. Enterprise data services (API, bulk export, custom datasets): QUOTE ONLY - 'price varies by data product and service method', contact hello@itjuzi.com. No enterprise figure is published; do not infer one.
ml_training_license: Unknown but the most promising posture in the China group. The existence of a productised custom-dataset business with MySQL/JSON delivery and named enterprise customers implies ITjuzi is willing to license data for internal systems use, which is the right commercial shape for a training licence. Whether AI/ML training specifically is permitted is NOT stated anywhere public - ask explicitly and get it in writing. Chinese cross-border data-transfer rules still apply and need qualified legal review.
language: Chinese (primary). An English 'About Us' exists; the data itself is Chinese.
update_frequency: Daily updates; enterprise incremental refresh selectable daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly.
fit_for_lead_prediction: The most ML-practical China source in this group, because it is the only one that openly advertises CSV/MySQL/JSON bulk delivery with incremental updates and field-level customisation - exactly what a training pipeline consumes. Its limits are scope and depth: TMT/new-economy only, ~2013 onward, and M&A is one event type among funding rounds rather than a curated deal database, so China industrial mid-market M&A is largely absent. Best used for China tech deal labels and investor-behaviour features; the CNY 798/yr membership is cheap enough to buy immediately just to assess data quality before negotiating an enterprise feed.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for membership; unknown for enterprise API/bulk (INFERRED low-to-mid based on Chinese market norms)

name: OpenDART (Financial Supervisory Service, Korea)
data_types: Korean statutory disclosure data via Open API - 23 API services across four groups: disclosure search (DS001), periodic-report key information (DS002), periodic-report financial information (DS003), and share/ownership status. Includes filing metadata and full original filing documents, listed-company financial statements, major shareholder and executive shareholding changes, capital increases/decreases, treasury shares, corporate governance, and - critically for M&A - merger, business transfer, split and share-exchange filings and public tender-offer documents. Approximately 7.2 million DART filings opened to external use.
coverage_geo: South Korea - all DART filers: KOSPI, KOSDAQ, KONEX listed companies plus unlisted companies with disclosure obligations (external-audit companies).
history_depth: DART/KRX disclosures from 1999 onward are available (per DeepSearch's description of its DART-sourced coverage). API-accessible window should be verified against the developer guide, but INFERRED to cover the full DART archive.
api: Yes - REST Open API with an issued authentication key (인증키). Free registration open to anyone: individuals, companies and institutions. Well-documented per-endpoint developer guides. Docs URL: https://opendart.fss.or.kr/guide/main.do (per-API guides e.g. https://opendart.fss.or.kr/guide/detail.do?apiGrpCd=DS001&apiId=2019001 ). Mature open-source client libraries exist: https://github.com/FinanceData/OpenDartReader (Python), https://github.com/seokhoonj/opendart (R).
bulk_delivery: Partial - no SFTP/S3, but disclosure-search plus document-acquisition endpoints permit systematic date-range harvesting into your own store, subject to call quotas. Original filing documents downloadable.
pricing: FREE. Terms Article 11 states that services provided by the FSS are in principle free of charge (with a reserved right to introduce charges if necessary). Source: https://opendart.fss.or.kr/intro/terms.do , observed 2026-09. Call quotas apply - Terms Article 10(4) states the Open API service has usage-count allowances which are posted on the website.
ml_training_license: Partly favourable, with a caveat. The terms do NOT explicitly prohibit commercial use; Article 20 restricts only uses contrary to public order and morals or intended to harm national or social public interest. However Article 16(1) asserts that COPYRIGHT in the Open API service and related programs belongs to the FSS, and Article 16(6) restricts excessive network access. There is NO explicit provision on redistribution or AI/ML training. INFERRED: internal analytical and model-training use of the underlying public filings is likely acceptable, but the copyright assertion means this should be confirmed with the FSS administrator and reviewed by qualified counsel before building a commercial product on it.
language: Korean (filing documents and most field labels). API guides are Korean.
update_frequency: Real time as filings are submitted; business-day cycle.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Korea's free equivalent of EDINET and the obvious first build for Korean coverage - zero licence cost, mature Python/R clients, and the filings include merger, business-transfer, split and tender-offer documents that give you dated M&A event labels, plus shareholding-change filings as a leading stake-building signal. Constraints are call quotas, Korean-language NLP, and an FSS copyright assertion with no explicit ML clause. Covers only disclosure-obligated companies, so Korea's smaller private targets are missing - pair with DeepSearch or THE VC for those.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) - free

update_frequency: Continuous automated collection; daily in practice.

Coverage is also venture/startup-centric and only ~2016 onward, missing Korean industrial mid-market M&A. Useful as an inexpensive Korean research and validation tool; for Korean training data go to OpenDART (free, full archive) or negotiate with DeepSearch.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr)

name: DeepSearch (딥서치) - Finorma API / DeepSearch AI / LISTING marketplace
data_types: Korean and US corporate/financial data: listed and unlisted company financials with 10-year history, real-time stock prices, news from 1,500 domestic media outlets (~30,000 articles/day), regulatory disclosures (DART and KRX from 1999), securities research reports, IR materials, patent records, earnings call transcripts, ETF data, credit ratings and bond ratings, shareholding/ownership structure, and revenue structure. Also operates LISTING, an actual M&A marketplace (cumulative transaction volume reported at over KRW 800 billion, ~4.7 acquisition offers per 30 days, 80% business-transaction matching success rate) and states its engine has supported over 2,000 M&A deals.

HKEX does provide programmatic data download for its paid historical data products. Third-party wrappers exist (Apify actors, R package https://rdrr.io/github/cskmlui/hkex.api/ , various GitHub scrapers) - these are NOT affiliated with HKEX and their own listings state as much.
bulk_delivery: Partial - paid HKEX historical data products support programmatic file download via API. Announcement text itself must be harvested from HKEXnews.
pricing: HKEXnews website access: FREE. HKEX historical data products: paid, priced per product with published discount structure - 15% discount for subscriptions of 12 consecutive months or longer, and a 50% academic discount on most historical data products used for academic research (excluding products already heavily price-reduced; availability flagged per product). Base per-product prices were not captured in this pass - consult the HKEX historical data product catalogue. Third-party alternative: an Apify actor reading the HKEXnews Titles Search API is listed from USD 150 per 1,000 disclosures (THIRD-PARTY, not HKEX, https://apify.com/nexgendata/hkex-news-announcements ) - note this unit economics gets expensive fast at corpus scale.
ml_training_license: Unknown for HKEXnews content specifically. INFERRED: the filings are statutory public disclosures, so internal analytical use is likely defensible, but HKEX asserts rights over its website content and market data products and its terms restrict systematic access - and scraping HKEXnews at volume risks blocking. Paid HKEX data products carry standard market-data licence terms that typically exclude redistribution. Verify with HKEX; do not rely on third-party scraper actors as a licensing route.
language: English and Traditional Chinese - Hong Kong issuers must file in both, which makes this the most language-accessible disclosure source in the Greater China region for an English-preferring pipeline.
update_frequency: Real time as announcements are published.
fit_for_lead_prediction: Genuinely useful and nearly free: Hong Kong filings are bilingual English/Chinese, cover ~2,600 issuers including many mainland-China companies, and the transaction-classification regime (VSA, VSD, discloseable and connected transactions) means deals arrive pre-tagged by materiality - unusually clean labels for an NLP extraction pipeline, and the 50% academic discount is worth probing if any research framing applies. Costs are engineering plus access risk: no official announcements API, so harvesting depends on an undocumented endpoint that HKEX may rate-limit or block. Covers listed issuers only.
budget_tier: low (<$10k/yr) for HKEXnews harvesting; unknown for paid HKEX historical data products
